summary.title: Build Your Lean Canvas in 5 Minutes | LEANSpark
summary.one_liner: Lean Canvas is a one-page business model template for testing a startup's riskiest assumptions, and this page describes LEANSpark, an AI tool that drafts the canvas and suggests what to validate first.
takeaways: Lean Canvas is a 12-block one-page template by Ash Maurya (2010) that adapts the Business Model Canvas for early-stage startups.

The 12 blocks include customer segments, problem, existing alternatives, unique value proposition, solution, key metrics, channels, early adopters, cost structure, revenue streams, unfair advantage, and high-level concept.
Lean Canvas swaps Key Partners, Key Activities, Key Resources and Customer Relationships from the BMC for Problem, Solution, Key Metrics and Unfair Advantage.
LEANSpark claims to build a canvas from a free-text idea description and stress-test it across 7 dimensions: Clarity, Desirability, Viability, Feasibility, Defensibility, Mission, and Timing.
The page lists paid tiers (Starter $25/month, Pro $50/month, Power $100/month) with a free first stress-test; the page does not explain the tiers beyond their stated goals.
summary.summary: This is a vendor landing page for LEANSpark, an AI tool that turns a plain-language business idea into a Lean Canvas and flags which assumptions to test first. Most of the page is marketing and pricing tiers, but it also includes an explanatory section on what Lean Canvas is, listing its 12 blocks and how it differs from the Business Model Canvas. The page says the tool is built by the creator of Lean Canvas, Ash Maurya, and that the methodology is part of Running Lean. Pricing is shown as $25, $50 and $100 per month for the paid steps, with a free initial stress test.
